embeds.title: HOW BLHA SCORING WORKS
embeds.description: The BLHA scoring system has two goals: every point should come from something the player actually controls, and no single stat should decide a matchup. Each value was set against NHL league-wide averages over the last three seasons (about 3 goals, 29 shots and a .900 save percentage per team per game), and the reasons are below.

fields.name: SKATERS
fields.value:
Goal **+5.00**
Assist **+2.97**
Shot on Goal **+0.53**
Block **+0.44**
Hit **+0.14**
Penalty Minute **−0.36**

fields.name: GOALIES
fields.value:
Game Started **+5.00**
Save **+0.56**
Goal Against **−5.00**
Goalie Goal **+5.00**
Goalie Assist **+2.97**

fields.name: **━━━ GOALS, ASSISTS, SHOTS ━━━**
fields.value:
**Equal weight.** NHL teams average about **1.7 assists** and about **9.4 shots** for every goal. The assist and shot values come straight from those ratios: 5.00 ÷ 1.69 ≈ **2.97**, and 5.00 ÷ 9.4 ≈ **0.53**.

So across the league, goals, assists and shots each add up to almost exactly the same share of points, about 15 per team per game each. Snipers, playmakers and high-volume shooters all have a real path to value, and no single build is the right one.

Shots carry that much weight on purpose. Shot volume is the most repeatable stat in hockey; a player's shooting percentage jumps around from year to year, but how often he shoots doesn't. Rewarding shots means a cold streak doesn't wipe out a player who's still creating chances.

fields.name: **━━━ BLOCKS AND HITS ━━━**
fields.value:
**The supporting cast.** Blocks and hits make up about **17%** of skater points. That's enough to make a shutdown defenseman or an energy-line banger worth a roster spot, and it means your six D slots aren't all about power-play points. It isn't enough for a 250-hit grinder to outscore a 30-goal winger.

A hit (0.14) is set so that, across the league, hits give back about what penalties take away. Blocks (0.44) carry the rest of that 17%. Teams throw about 21 hits a game and block about 15 shots, and hit totals depend a lot on which arena's scorer is counting. Blocks are the more consistent stat, so each one counts for more.

fields.name: **━━━ PENALTY MINUTES ━━━**
fields.value:
**Penalized on the ice, penalized on your roster.** A penalty hurts a real team by handing the other side a power play. Over the last three seasons, NHL teams scored about **0.07 power-play goals for every penalty minute** taken against them. At 5.00 a goal, that's **0.36 per minute**.

That rate counts every minute, including offsetting minors, fighting majors and misconducts that never create a power play, so those minutes are already priced in. Fantrax counts only total minutes, and this is the fairest rate for a minute of any kind.

Minor → **−0.72**
Fighting major → **−1.80**
10-minute misconduct → **−3.60**

Across the league, penalties take back about what hits add. A clean player loses almost nothing; an enforcer's hits no longer carry him.

fields.name: **━━━ GOALIES ━━━**
fields.value:
**Paid to start, judged on stopping.** A goal against costs exactly what a goal is worth (**−5.00**), so a goal counts the same at both ends of the ice.

The save value (0.56) puts the break-even point at the league-average save percentage, about **.900**. A goalie stopping shots at a better rate than average earns points on every shot he faces, and one below it loses points. An average goalie scores the same whether he faces 20 shots or 40, so a flood of shots only helps a goalie who is actually stopping them.

The **5.00** start bonus makes an average start worth playing. A league-average night (about 29 shots at .900) scores about **5.1**, around 1.7 times an average skater's game.

fields.name: WHAT A START CAN LOOK LIKE
fields.value:
28 saves on 30 shots → **+10.68**
30-save shutout → **+21.80**
20 saves on 25 shots (5 goals against) → **−8.80**

fields.name: **━━━ WHAT ISN'T SCORED ━━━**
fields.value:
**Wins:** decided by the skaters in front of him and the other team's goalie. Saves and goals against measure the goalie himself.
**Shutouts:** already rewarded, because a shutout has zero goals against. A bonus would count it twice.
**Plus/minus:** a team stat that swings on who else is on the ice.
**Power-play points and game-winning goals:** those goals and assists already count. A bonus double-counts them or rewards luck.
**Faceoffs:** only centers take them, so they'd tip the value of the C slot and the F flex spot.

fields.name: **━━━ WHY THE ODD DECIMALS ━━━**
fields.value: 2.97, 0.53, 0.44, 0.14, 0.36 and 0.56 come from the averages above, rounded, so they aren't arbitrary. Off-round values have a bonus too: an exact tie in a weekly matchup becomes almost impossible.

fields.name: **━━━ FOR YOUR ROSTER ━━━**
fields.value:
Goal and 4 shots → **7.12**
Assist, 3 shots and a hit → **4.70**
Defenseman with no points, 2 shots, 3 blocks and 2 hits → **2.66**

Scoring is still king, but shooters and two-way defensemen stay in your lineup on nights the puck doesn't go in. Over a week, goalies average roughly a tenth of your total, but no other position can swing a matchup by 30 points in a single night.
